HubSpot (HUBS) stock is worth a fresh look after falling 50.0% from its highest close of the past year of $405.83 on December 30, 2025. HubSpot's free cash flow over the last twelve months now equals 6.7% of its market value, against 4.2% for the median S&P 500 company. That yield marks either a business on sale or one the market expects to shrink. So is HubSpot a business on sale, or a shrinking one?

HubSpot's Free Cash Flow Has Grown For Three Years

So far, HubSpot's cash profile resembles that of a business on sale. Its twelve-month free cash flow climbed from $243 million in the period ended September 2023 to $677 million in the period ended September 2026, and it was higher at every quarter end in between.

This matters to an owner. Shareholders own a slice of the free cash a business produces, whether paid out or not, just as they own a slice of its profit. When the market recognizes cash retained inside a company, the share price tends to follow, especially when that cash is growing.

HubSpot sells its software by subscription, and that software costs little to deliver: the company kept 83.0% of its revenue as gross profit over the last twelve months, against 77.3% at Salesforce. Its capital spending took 25.3% of the cash its operations brought in. HubSpot turned 18.9% of its revenue into free cash flow, against 17.3% at Microsoft. Three other peers turned more: 34.5% at Salesforce, 20.1% at IBM and 40.8% at Adobe.

Reported profit is thinner: HubSpot's operating margin was 5.4% over the last twelve months, up from a loss of 1.6% of revenue a year earlier. HubSpot's stock-based compensation over the same twelve months was $504 million, about 14% of its $3.59 billion of revenue. And HubSpot does not need its cash to pay down borrowing: at the end of September 2026 it held $1.30 billion of cash and short-term investments, against $224 million of debt.

Why Is HubSpot's Growth Slowing?

HubSpot's growth is slowing because customers are taking longer to buy, management said on the November 4, 2026 call. Revenue growth from a year earlier fell in the second and third quarters of 2026, from 23.4% in fiscal Q1 2026 to 19.8% in fiscal Q2 and 17.1% in fiscal Q3. Management expects growth of 12% for fiscal Q4 2026.

Management says customers are buying differently in the AI era. They want to test AI on their own data before they pay, and HubSpot's move to free trials and pricing tied to outcomes has lengthened buying cycles. Larger customers bring more decision-makers into each deal, while smaller ones are more sensitive to price.

AI-related stocks have faced notable selling pressure recently, with several developments weighing on sentiment. But while the market's attitude has gone sour, the reality remains that the underlying growth outlook is highly favorable for many companies directly benefiting from the revolution, with recent results from several underpinning the favorable picture.

Nebius Group NBIS, Snowflake SNOW, and Salesforce CRM have all recently posted strong results, with each currently sporting a favorable Zacks Rank, reflecting bullish earnings pictures.

Nebius Growth Remains Explosive

Nebius, a current Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), provides AI-focused cloud infrastructure, offering the computing capacity companies need to develop, train, and deploy advanced AI models. Shares have faced notable pressure recently, with concerns surrounding massive capital expenditures and financing needs weighing heavily.

EPS revisions have soared across the board over recent months.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Negative sentiment aside, the growth picture remains remarkably strong, with revenue in its latest release soaring 571% YoY to $981 million. Importantly, management expects 2027 sales in the $12-$13 billion range, roughly quadruple 2026 revenue.

The company's massive spending requirements do remain a concern, helping explain the weak post-earnings reaction and overall negative sentiment. But while the spending picture is undoubtedly aggressive, robust demand for AI infrastructure provides a favorable longer-term backdrop.

Snowflake Continues Benefiting From AI Adoption

Snowflake, a current Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), provides a cloud-based data platform that enables enterprises to store, analyze, and increasingly utilize their information for AI applications. EPS revisions for its current and next fiscal years have climbed consistently over the past year, suggesting growth rates of 78% in FY27 and 33% in FY28.

Its latest quarterly results were rock-solid and reflected big growth, with sales of $1.6 billion growing 35% from the same period last year. The demand picture also remained favorable, with remaining performance obligations climbing 30% YoY to $9 billion. And to top it off, net revenue retention of 126% further reflected continued spending growth among existing customers.

Zacks Investment Research

Salesforce's AI Momentum Remains Strong

Salesforce, a current Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), has become an increasingly prominent AI player through its Agentforce platform, which enables businesses to deploy autonomous AI agents to automate workflows, improve customer interactions, and boost productivity.

After years of unconditionally backing Jensen Huang and Nvidia (NASDAQ), Jim Cramer's confidence in the chipmaker has been shaken by the controversy surrounding its chief executive. And the reasons are understandable.

Cramer's investment thesis on Nvidia has always been closely tied to Huang's leadership. The CNBC host has repeatedly praised Huang as a visionary capable of transforming entire industries through artificial intelligence. He believed so strongly in Nvidia that he even named his dog after the company in 2017.

But with Huang's future now uncertain following allegations involving a suspected Chinese spy, Cramer's longtime conviction is facing a serious test. The controversy has raised questions about Huang's reputation and whether he can continue leading the company.

Cramer recently downgraded Nvidia from a buy to a hold, citing uncertainty surrounding the investigation.

Billionaires Ray Dalio and Philippe Laffont both trimmed their Nvidia stakes in the second quarter, even before this controversy began. See which AI stocks they still own.

That doesn't mean Cramer has turned bearish on the entire stock market (see what Cramer was buying last week).

While the Nvidia controversy and concerns about massive AI infrastructure spending have made him increasingly cautious, Cramer believes there are still plenty of attractive investment opportunities elsewhere.

During the recent CNBC Investing Club's annual meeting, Cramer and portfolio director Jeff Marks reviewed over 30 stocks in the Club's portfolio, identifying several companies they remain bullish on. Cramer has also continued to highlight investment opportunities outside the increasingly volatile AI trade.

Against this backdrop, we take a look at 10 stocks Jim Cramer is bullish on, ranked by the number of hedge funds holding stakes in them at the end of the second quarter of 2026.

Before this controversy, two well-known billionaires were backing Nvidia as an AI stock. See who they are.

You can click to read our full list on Jim Cramer Is Bullish on These 10 Stocks Amid Nvidia Controversy. The top 5 stocks from that list are mentioned below.

Methodology

To pick the stocks, we went through CNBC's coverage of Jim Cramer's latest stock picks, mainly the reports on his CNBC Investing Club annual meeting. From that coverage, we selected 5 stocks that Cramer is bullish on. We then ranked them by the number of hedge funds holding stakes in each one at the end of the second quarter of 2026, using Insider Monkey's database of 1,000+ hedge funds.

Zeta Global Holdings ZETA is pairing faster revenue growth with rising artificial intelligence usage and improving cash generation. Management raised its 2026 revenue outlook after another quarter of accelerating organic growth, giving growth-oriented investors a stronger operating case.

Valuation remains the counterweight. ZETA trades at 31.3X forward 12-month earnings, versus 18.98X for the Zacks sub-industry and 18.8X for the S&P 500. That premium increases the importance of sustained execution.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

ZETA's Revenue Growth Supports the Bull Case

Management now expects 2026 revenues of $1.853-$1.857 billion, with the $1.855 billion midpoint implying 42% growth. Excluding mergers and acquisitions and political candidate revenues, the company expects 27% growth for the year.

Customer metrics reinforce that outlook. Super-scaled customers increased 18% year over year to 212 in the third quarter, while super-scaled customer average revenue per user rose 22% to $2 million. Both measures accelerated from the preceding quarter, showing that growth is coming from customer additions and deeper platform usage.

Zeta's AI Strategy Is Showing Commercial Traction

Athena adoption is becoming more visible in customer economics. More than 50% of super-scaled customers were monthly active Athena users, while Athena adopters represented more than 70% of revenues. The top 25 Athena users generated revenue growth above 70% year over year in the third quarter, well ahead of Zeta's overall 46% growth.

AthenaOS and Zeta Business Intelligence are designed to extend the platform beyond marketing into broader enterprise decisioning. Salesforce, Inc. CRM is also embedding AI agents into marketing workflows through Agentforce Marketing. Adobe Inc. ADBE has expanded its customer-experience platform with agentic AI capabilities, underscoring the competitive push to combine enterprise data, automation and decision support.

ZETA's Cash Flow Strength Expands Flexibility

Third-quarter operating cash flow increased 57.7% year over year to $91.3 million, while free cash flow advanced 73% to $81.5 million. Free cash flow margin reached 16.5%, reflecting stronger conversion of growth into cash.

Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance to $270.6-$271.6 million, implying growth of 64-65%. Higher cash generation gives Zeta more room to fund product development and acquisitions while supporting share repurchases. The company had repurchased $101.4 million of shares through Nov. 9.

Zoom Communications (ZM) stock rose 7.9% on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 1.3%. The day before, on November 10, the company launched an AI Launchpad program for startups. On November 11 itself, technology stocks rose broadly, and the sector fund XLK gained 3.2%. What did Zoom offer those startups, and where does AI already show up in its sales?

Zoom Offered AI Startups Free Credits

Zoom said on November 10 that its AI Launchpad gives AI-native startups up to $150,000 in complimentary credits to build apps on its speech, language, and voice AI services, with no equity stake required. The shares slipped 0.9% that day.

AI already shows up in Zoom's Enterprise business. On its August 25, 2026 call, management said Enterprise revenue grew 7.8% in fiscal Q2 2027, its strongest rate in three years, against 4.9% for total revenue. It said the pickup came from its work on AI for the workplace, AI-first customer experience and new AI products. One of those products is Zoom Virtual Agent, whose customer count grew more than 250% from a year earlier, management said on the same call.

Zoom Rose Far More Than Software Stocks

Zoom gained far more than other software stocks on November 11, though most of them rose as well. The median of the 63 other application software companies worth $2 billion or more gained 1.2%, with 46 of them rising. Three of those companies rose 5% or more, as Zoom did.

Technology stocks led the market that day. The technology sector fund XLK gained 3.2%, and U.S. stocks rose after CoreWeave's earnings update eased worries that AI profits would not come soon enough to cover infrastructure debt. Four of Zoom's five peers rose, among them RingCentral at 2.4%, while Microsoft fell 2.3%. Zoom's gain was more than six times the application software median.

Where Zoom Stock Stands Now

A rise like this is not rare for Zoom. The stock had five rises at least this large in the prior 365 days, the latest being a 9.9% gain on June 1, 2026. Over the past twelve months, it returned 17.9%, against 12.8% for the S&P 500.

Shares closed at $98.08, remaining below their 52-week closing high of $111.88 set on June 2, 2026. The 52-week closing low was $72.72 on March 2, 2026. In the three months to November 11, the stock lost 10.7%, compared with a 2.0% fall for the S&P 500.

On sales, Zoom costs more than the market, trading at 5.8 times sales against 3.2 for the S&P 500. Zoom is expected to report its fiscal third-quarter 2027 results later in November 2026, and the measure to watch is Enterprise revenue growth.
